title: Console VPC Wizard — axioms, happy path, and edge-case checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the UX axioms, step-by-step wireframe intentions, and a practical edge-case checklist for the Private Deployments admin console VPC/Region/KMS onboarding wizard.

Audience:
- Product managers and PM-design leads
- Console UX designers
- Solutions engineers (customer onboarding)
- Eng triage: infra & private-deploy runtime owners

Status:
Working draft. Intentionally pragmatic (checklists + copy + acceptance criteria). Not final UI; meant to reduce back-and-forth with eng during grooming.

Design axioms (guiding principles):
1) Minimize blast radius: break VPC setup into reversible steps; never create permanent infra without explicit final confirmation.
2) Defaults that minimize support: pre-validate region + subnet combos; surface only compatible options by default.
3) Progressive disclosure: show advanced network/HSM toggles behind a collapsible section.
4) Fast failure and clear remediation: when validation fails, show exact API/console commands customers can run and a single click to re-run validations.
5) Auditability: every step logs a human-readable change summary for customers and for SRE (downloadable).

Happy-path user flow (high level):
1) Start wizard: user selects "Create private deployment" -> "VPC + Region".
2) Select region: dropdown lists regions where we have Private control plane + available capacity. Regions marked with SLA tier.
3) Choose network option: (a) Redwood-managed network (simpler) OR (b) Bring-your-own VPC (BYOVPC).
4) If BYOVPC: input VPC ID, CIDR, and list of subnets per availability zone. Attach optional route table IDs for peering.
5) CIDR and subnet validation runs asynchronously; results show green checks with latency estimate for provisioning.
6) KMS/HSM step: choose customer-managed key (external KMS via IAM role) OR Redwood-managed key. For HSM, collect certificate + endpoint, show hardware requirement checks.
7) Review summary page: shows cost impact estimate, latency delta note (if cross-region), and rollback checkbox (default on).
8) Confirm and provision. Post-provision screen shows next steps, quick links to network peering docs, and a validity window for test tokens.

Wireframe notes / UI copy snippets: (for designers)
- Region selector label: "Deployment region (where inference nodes will run)"
- Region help tooltip: "Select a region with dedicated capacity for Private Deployments. Choosing a different region may increase latency or cost."
- Network option toggle: "Redwood-managed network (recommended)" / "Use my VPC (advanced)"
- BYOVPC field helper: "VPC must allow TCP 443 egress to control-plane.redwood.com and must not use overlapping CIDRs with existing Redwood-managed networks."
- KMS option subheading: "Encryption at rest: choose a key we manage or bring your own."
- HSM block: "HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) — enterprise only. Contact sales for hardware-backed cluster placement."

Validation rules and UX behaviors: (grooming-to-engineering)
- CIDR/subnet syntax validation client-side.
- Cross-account role detection: if a supplied KMS ARN is in another account, surface exact IAM policy snippet and button to copy to clipboard.
- Async validations: back-end job id returned; front-end polls with exponential backoff and shows ETA.
- If network peering is required, provide a one-click "generate peering request" that exports a JSON blob customers can upload to their cloud console.

Edge-case checklist (must be covered in acceptance tests):
- Overlapping CIDR with existing Redwood deployments -> show "Conflict: overlapping with deployment XYZ" and offer remediation steps.
- Subnet in region without GPU capacity -> warn and recommend alternative region; allow override with risk acknowledgement.
- Partial permission principle: customer’s IAM role can validate resources but cannot perform changes; wizard must gracefully fall back to "manual steps" mode with clear copy.
- KMS key policy missing encrypt/decrypt for runtime role -> show single-click policy snippet and how to attach.
- HSM endpoint unreachable from control plane -> show diagnostic command (curl with TLS fingerprint) and a boolean "tested" toggle to proceed only after manual triage.
- Long-running validations (timeouts) -> auto-cancel after 20 minutes and persist partial results; allow user to resume.
- Mistyped identifiers -> fuzzy-match suggestions (e.g., suggest vpc-1234 when user typed vpc-1243).
- Region mismatch between control plane and requested compute -> block unless user explicitly selects cross-region deployment with explained SLA differences.

Operational considerations (SRE / infra notes):
- All wizard actions should emit structured events to the observability pipeline: wizard.step.start, wizard.validation.fail, wizard.provision.complete with metadata (region, vpc_id).
- Retain validation logs for 30 days for debugging onboarding issues.
- Provide a "replay validation" endpoint that solutions-eng can call when troubleshooting.

Acceptance criteria (for feature completion):
- UI implements the full happy-path with validated region list and Redwood-managed vs BYOVPC toggle.
- Asynchronous validation flow implemented and tested for all listed validations.
- KMS/HSM options present, with copy+policy snippets and clear error remediation flows.
- Edge cases above documented and smoke-tested in staging with at least three mock tenant accounts.
- UX microcopy finalized and approved by legal for KMS/HSM compliance claims.

Backlog and proposed tickets (rough sizing):
- RINF-872: VPC Wizard skeleton + region selector (3 days)
- RINF-873: BYOVPC validation engine + CIDR conflicts (5 days)
- RINF-874: KMS integration UI + IAM policy generator (4 days)
- RINF-875: HSM diagnostic step + certificate upload (4 days)
- RINF-876: Export peering JSON + one-click helper (2 days)
- RINF-877: Observability events + retention policy (2 days)

Open questions / decisions needed: (to discuss in next grooming)
- Scope of Redwood-managed network: do we create peering automatically or always ask for customer acceptance?
- SLA messaging: how do we surface cross-region latency expectations numerically? Who signs off on copy?
- HSM availability: which partners/providers do we officially support at launch?

Notes to self / TODO before design review:
- Create a short video demo of the wizard happy path (30–60s).
- Mock the async validations with synthetic latencies to check spinner behavior.
- Ask legal for final KMS/HSM claim language.

Slack refs and context: 
- See thread: #prod-private-deploys thread 2024-09-09 (link in linked_artifacts).
- Quick ask to solutions-eng @Priya: confirm steps we can automate for peering creation.

Appendix: sample IAM policy snippet for cross-account KMS allow (copyable):
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodRuntimeEncryptDecrypt",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDDIT:role/redwood-runtime" },
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
